assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, above all reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis, rests on nucleotide chemistry: engineered dNTP analogues, polymerase behaviour and single-molecule detection. It turned DNA sequencing into a routine tool and reshaped genetics, cancer genomics and diagnostics. From my own field of nucleotide metabolism and replication fidelity, I see it as a clear chemical invention with very broad effect.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman are the core of the Solexa chemistry and the clonal-array concept. Rothberg's pyrosequencing-in-picowells platform is the other early commercial route. Pascal Mayer and Jingyue Ju also made real contributions, and the pyrosequencing priority of others lies outside the supplied names, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of use, many independent platforms, and a clinical and research footprint beyond dispute. Recognition is timely or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Sequencing was already recognised in 1980 (Sanger, Gilbert), so the committee may see this as an incremental technology step.
Credit split between sequencing-by-synthesis and pyrosequencing, and the exclusion of non-credited pioneers, is unresolved.
I have not verified patent or priority details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation introduced a new pharmacological principle: small molecules that recruit E3 ligases to destroy chosen proteins. Heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues such as the thalidomide analogues and their cereblon mechanism are now in clinical trials. The concept came out of chemical biology and has changed how drug discovery is approached.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains the molecular glue mechanism. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito are also important. The credit across PROTACs and glues is multi-part, and a three-person split leaves out strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for the concept and the cereblon mechanism, with many independent confirmations. Clinical validation of PROTACs is still emerging, so the timing is borderline-early for that half.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two needing separate recognition.
Clinical success of degraders is not yet established beyond early-phase data as far as I know.
Ito's role next to Handa is hard to separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made practical delivery of siRNA and mRNA possible, and they underlie the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and the first siRNA drug approvals. The impact is large and the chemistry (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, formulation by controlled mixing) is real and distinct.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and his group (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) built the ionizable-lipid LNP technology. Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries. Credit is spread over many people and a pharmaceutical-chemistry commons; the 2023 Medicine prize already recognised the nucleoside modifications for mRNA, which affects how the prize would be framed.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been proven in billions of doses and in an approved siRNA drug. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA vaccines.
Decisive inventorship among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is difficult to assign.
Not clear whether the committee treats this as chemistry or as pharmaceutical technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The idea that biomolecular condensates form by liquid-liquid phase separation introduced a new organising principle for cell biology and linked it to physical chemistry. It has prompted a very large body of work, including on nucleotide-binding and replication-stress condensates.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman reported the liquid P granule behaviour in 2009. Rosen showed multivalent phase separation in vitro in 2012. Pappu and Mittag supply the physical-chemical theory. A three-person grouping is plausible but leaves out important theory contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concept widely adopted, but the physiological relevance of phase separation in cells remains debated, and many findings are not well controlled. Possibly early.
uncertainties: Disagreement over how general in vivo phase separation is and over how it should be tested.
Chemistry versus cell biology classification.
Allocation between experimentalists and theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's chemical genetics of kinases (analogue-sensitive alleles) and, more notably, the discovery that mutant KRAS G12C can be covalently targeted through the switch-II pocket reversed a view of KRAS as undruggable. The work led to approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib). It is chemically elegant and clinically consequential.
assessment.attribution: Attribution to a single laureate is clean for the KRAS cysteine-targeting work and the kinase chemical genetics. Companies (Araxes, Amgen, Mirati) developed the drugs but the decisive concept is Shokat's.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple clinical agents and structural studies. Timely.
uncertainties: Single-laureate prize is unusual and the committee may prefer to pair it with another discovery.
Resistance and limited durability of KRAS G12C inhibitors may temper enthusiasm, though not the conceptual contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks by chemically modifying nucleobases with deaminases. They are used widely in research and in the first clinical applications. I see it as a chemistry-driven refinement of genome editing.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor (CBE) and Gaudelli (ABE) as first authors who carried out the key work. The alternatives from Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) are independent but less decisive.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are early but encouraging, and the method is widely replicated. Likely premature for a prize this soon after CRISPR (2020), or at least better combined with prime editing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Relationship to prime editing (B068) for a single prize.
Whether Komor and Gaudelli would be named or Liu alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible methylation of mRNA adenosines (m6A), with writers, erasers and readers, established a new layer of gene regulation, the epitranscriptome. I find it close to my own interests in nucleotide chemistry, and it has opened a large field of research with therapeutic angles.
assessment.attribution: He proposed the reversible-modification concept and the FTO demethylase mechanism. Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini and Meyer) mapped m6A transcriptome-wide. Jia and Yang also identified FTO activity. Allocation among many strong contributors is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Widely validated, but quantitative mapping methods and some functional claims are still being revised. Slightly early.
uncertainties: Dispute over mapping accuracy and specificity of m6A-seq and antibodies.
Priority for FTO as an m6A demethylase.
Seems more molecular biology than chemistry to some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics, covering shotgun sequencing, quantitative and targeted methods, made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and their modifications in cells. The effect on biology and medicine is very large.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the usual core trio, with Hunt, Gygi and Heck as additional leading contributors. The 2002 prize recognised the ionisation methods themselves, so a new prize would honour the proteome-scale methodology.
assessment.maturity: Mature and heavily used, so recognition is timely or even late.
uncertainties: Method development is spread over many people, so the trio is a judgement.
Possible overlap in the committee's mind with the 2002 mass spectrometry prize.
